title: skillwright architecture: build a marketplace model, then translate it per harness?
summary: How skillwright is built today (structure and the build, check and publish flows), where the harness knowledge sits, and whether to move to a load → model → translate → emit pipeline.

blocks.title: The question
blocks.text:
Your proposal: build a data representation of the whole marketplace first, then emit it through a translator per harness.

Today there is **no marketplace model**. `build`/`check` (`export.rs`) and `publish` (`publish.rs`) are two separate pipelines. Each one reads notes, compiles them and writes bytes in one pass, and each pass already knows which harness it is writing for. The only grouping is `PluginGroup`: borrowed lists of discovered notes, with no compiled content in them.

Why it matters now: adding a harness or a component kind means editing both pipelines and about five separate tables of harness facts. `publish` can only write a plugin for Claude and Codex, while `build` supports four harnesses. That gap is a symptom of the split.

Constraints any answer has to keep:
- The core stays I/O-free above `Vfs`, so it still runs as wasm (Obsidian, TS).
- `check` must never disagree with `build`. Today that holds because both render into a `PreviewVfs`.
- Refusal tokens and the byte-for-byte output of the committed `plugin/` trees must not change. CI diffs them.
- The `sw-` strip and the rail against writing into the vault both stay.

Files read: `tradecraft-core/src/{lib,export,publish,compile,projection,discover,vault,content,frontmatter,vfs,authoring,status,manifest,guard}.rs`, `skillwright/src/{cli,lib}.rs`, `skillwright/src/commands/*`, `tradecraft-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `plugin/skillwright.yaml`.

blocks.title: Layers and modules
blocks.alt: Layer diagram: hosts (CLI, wasm, typegen) over tradecraft-core (read, transform, render+write, plan, projection, rails), over the Vfs seam, over the osdlc library crates, over the output trees. Orange boxes hold harness facts.
blocks.caption: Orange = holds harness-specific facts. The render+write box holds two pipelines.
blocks.detail: The core is cleanly layered on its inputs. Discover/vault/frontmatter all read into typed structs, and `authoring` already uses decide-then-execute: it returns an `AuthoringOp` and the host applies it. The output side has no such split. `export` and `publish` decide what to write and write it in the same function.

nodes.title: skillwright (CLI)
nodes.detail: Flags → request → one core call → report. `commands/harness/adapter.rs` holds a separate harness table for the install/update CLIs.

blocks.title: Sketch: a HarnessProfile (data) and a HarnessTranslator (code) per harness
blocks.caption: Built from today's `RootSpec` (export.rs), `PluginLayout` and the target functions (publish.rs), and `Adapter` (skillwright harness/adapter.rs). The fields are the union of those tables; nothing new is invented.

blocks.title: What the review found
blocks.text:
1. **Your direction fits the code.** The input side already produces typed data (`DiscoveredComponent`, `VaultNote`, `VaultFrontmatter`). `authoring` already separates deciding from doing. `PreviewVfs` already makes check = build. What is missing is the middle: a compiled, harness-neutral `Marketplace` value.
2. **Compile is where harness knowledge gets in too early.** `compile_projection` turns `/[[call]]` into a harness's call string, so it needs a per-root `CallContext`. That is why `export` reads and compiles each note once per root. A model needs bodies that keep calls and links as references, rendered later by the translator.
3. **Two pipelines, one job.** `publish`'s plugin branch (`project_plugin`) re-does grouping, admission and manifests with its own layout table. That is how publish ended up supporting only 2 harnesses for packs.
4. **Harness facts are in about 8 places** (table above). A translator architecture needs one `HarnessProfile` per harness that every stage reads.
5. **Keep as is:** the Vfs seam, the rails in `guard`, the manifest's two hashes, refusal tokens, and status-as-dry-run. These belong in the Emit stage and do not need to change.

blocks.title: Proposed structure
blocks.alt: Pipeline diagram: Vault → 1 Load → 2 Marketplace model (marketplace, plugins, skills with segment bodies, commands, hooks, assets; validated, serializable) → 3 Translate, one translator per harness from one HarnessProfile row, producing a pure FileTree → 4 Emit (build swap, check diff, publish to destination with manifest, status dry-run). Adopt and authoring read and plan against the model.
blocks.caption: Each stage hands a value to the next. Only Load and Emit touch the Vfs.

blocks.title: Harness-specific additions in the model
blocks.text:
Each model node (skill, command, plugin, marketplace) has three layers of data:

1. **Common fields:** name, description, body, arguments, allowed tools. Every translator reads these.
2. **Extensions, per harness:** e.g. Claude's `disable-model-invocation`. Today they come from `sw-overrides` in frontmatter and are validated against `accepted_override_keys`. Only that harness's translator reads them.
3. **Annotations:** unknown non-`sw-` keys, passed through as written (today's carry rule).

**A current bug this fixes:** `sw-overrides` is applied by `publish` but not by `build`, so a Claude-only field reaches `.claude/skills` and goes missing from the built marketplace.

criteria.title: Low cost to make the change
Adding a harness or kind is one change
build, publish and status cannot disagree

scores.reason: A few days: merge the tables into one HarnessProfile.
export and publish together are ~13k lines including tests.
Still two render paths to extend.
The committed plugin/ trees and test snapshots act as a byte-for-byte oracle, which brings the risk down.

questions.prompt: Which architecture should skillwright move to?

options.title: Keep the pipelines; merge harness facts into one HarnessProfile table
options.detail: Cheapest, and it fixes the scattered tables. It leaves two renderers, per-root recompiles and the publish/build gap (packs only for claude and codex).

options.title: Model + translators for build/check only; publish stays as is
options.detail: Proves the model on the verb with the strongest oracle (the committed plugin/ trees). publish keeps its own renderer, so the two can still drift. A reasonable first step but not a place to stop.

options.title: Model + translators for every verb (load → model → translate → emit)
options.detail: Your proposal. Recommended: the inputs and the emit side are already in good shape, so the work is mostly moving compile's harness decisions into translators and deleting `project_plugin`. It can be phased: build/check first, then publish on the same translators.

questions.prompt: How should calls and links be represented once the model is loaded?

options.title: Two-phase load: resolve links and calls to model nodes; translators only spell them
options.detail: Recommended. Pass 1 reads every note into a node. Pass 2 resolves each [[link]] and /[[call]] against those nodes and stores a reference to the target; broken ones become validation errors on the model. The body is text with those resolved references in it. A translator does not decide validity, only spelling: /plugin:skill on Claude, plugin-skill on Pi, refused where sw-targets narrows the target out of that harness. This also replaces the string rewrites in render_skill.

options.title: A string with placeholder tokens filled in at translate time
options.detail: Smaller change to compile.rs, but tokens can collide with author text and a second lexer pass is needed to find them again.

options.title: Keep compiling per harness; the model holds one body per harness
options.detail: No change to compile.rs, but the model is no longer harness-neutral and you still compile N times.

questions.prompt: How should harness extensions be typed in the model?

options.title: A validated key/value map per harness, checked against that harness's accepted keys
options.detail: Recommended. It matches today's sw-overrides and the agent-adapt capability matrix. Adding a field is a table change, not a type change, and it serializes cleanly to wasm.

options.title: A typed struct per harness (ClaudeSkillExt, CodexSkillExt, ...)
options.detail: Compile-time checks and better docs, but every new harness field becomes a code change in core plus a typegen update.

options.title: Typed for the fields skillwright acts on, a map for the rest
options.detail: Typed where the translator makes decisions from a field (e.g. naming, hooks). Map for plain pass-through. More rules to explain.

questions.prompt: Where should the per-harness facts (the HarnessProfile rows) live?

options.title: One Rust HarnessProfile table in core, with links to harness-reference facts
options.detail: Recommended. Typed, compiled into wasm, and checked by tests. A test can assert that each row's sourced fields match a harness-reference fact, so the docs and code stay in sync.

options.title: Generate the table from harness-reference/bundle at build time
options.detail: Single source, but behavior (how a call is spelled, the shim rewrite) is code, not data, so part of each harness stays in Rust anyway.

options.title: Push it all into agent-adapt
options.detail: agent-adapt already owns per-runtime rendering. But marketplace layout and install CLIs are skillwright concepts, so this widens agent-adapt's scope.

questions.prompt: How much of a translator is data (the profile) and how much is per-harness code?

options.title: Data only: one generic translator driven by the profile
options.detail: Adding a harness would mean adding a row. But manifest JSON shapes, Cursor's hook rules and Pi's package.json are code, so the profile ends up full of enums that each switch into code, which is how today's PluginDialect works.

options.title: Profile + one HarnessTranslator trait with shared default methods
options.detail: Recommended. The defaults do the common work from the profile: narrowing, naming, skill placement, writing calls and links. Each harness overrides only what is code for it, mostly manifests and hook rules. A new harness is a profile plus a few methods.

options.title: One hand-written translator per harness, sharing helper functions
options.detail: Each translator is easy to read on its own, but the common rules (sw-targets narrowing, calls) are copied four times and can drift. That is today's export/publish problem, moved.

questions.prompt: Should the Marketplace model be a public, serialized contract (wasm, --json, Obsidian)?

options.title: Yes: exported through tradecraft-wasm and typegen
options.detail: Lets the Obsidian plugin show the whole marketplace and its per-harness results without re-implementing discovery. It becomes an API to keep stable.

options.title: Not yet: internal to core until it settles
options.detail: Free to change while the refactor lands. Can be exported later.

questions.prompt: Should adopt become the reverse of a translator (harness files → model → notes)?

options.title: Yes, in scope
options.detail: Symmetric and it would let adopt read Cursor/Pi layouts too. It makes the refactor bigger.

options.title: Later, separate work
options.detail: adopt.rs works today and does not block the forward path.
